```{r include=FALSE}
## 1. Read in Pertinent TCS Files for Placement Analysis: 'cases', 'charges', 'dispositions', and 'placements'

# set sharepoint path using csgjcr::csg_sp_path function
sharepoint_tcs_data_path <- csg_sp_path("JC Research - JJ_Michigan - JJ_Michigan/Data/Raw/Courts/JIS/TCS")

# import cases
tcs_cases <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_Cases_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

# import charges
tcs_charges <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_Charges_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

# import dispositions
tcs_dispositions <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_DispositionsPerCharge_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

# # import sentencing -- this is "Sentencing results on adult criminal FJ and DJ sentencings."
# tcs_sentencing <- read_xlsx(
#   file.path(
#     csg_path, "TCS_Sentencings_A.xlsx"),
#   .name_repair = make_clean_names
#   ) %>%
#   mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

# import placements
tcs_placements <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_Placements_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

```

```{r include=FALSE}
## 2. De-dup/figure out primary keys for 'cases', 'charges', 'dispositions', and 'placements' and merge together

# * `juvenile_nbr` (unique individual ID) and `case_number` (unique case ID, though not sure of "case" definition) appear to be main primary key across files, but will need to use dates at the very least to create pre- and post- disposition/adjudication distinctions in placement data *
# 
# * maybe also use `jurist_nbr` ("The professional number associated to the Judge assigned to the case."), either `case_year` or `year`, `tc_sreport_court_jcl` ("AS400 caseload report court code."),
# 
# **seemingly important dates:**
# 
# * offense_dt
# * case_file_dt
# * adjudication_dt
# * arraignment_dt
# * disposition
# * case_reopen_dt
# * case_closed_dt


# de-dup cases file -- there is a very slight discrepancy in N size when de-duping by only juvenile_nbr and case_number as opposed to also including one or more of the above dates; keeping as juvenile_nbr and case_number makes most intuitive sense pending confirmation from JIS contacts (also de-duping by offense_dt as we may need this for later joins...)
tcs_cases_de_dup <- tcs_cases %>%
  filter(!is.na(juvenile_nbr)==TRUE,
         juvenile_nbr!=0, ### there are a handful of records where juvenile_nbr=0; appears to be data error as the records don't consistently share other identifying info like dates and county
         !is.na(case_number)==TRUE) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_nbr,case_number,offense_dt,.keep_all = TRUE)

# de-dup charges file -- using case_id (same as 'case_number' in tcs_cases and 'id' (which is "Unique ID for the record.")); no records dropped

# issue: there are 1,288 records in the cases df that do not appear at all in the charges df; further there is no juvenile_nbr in the charges data which is concerning for the merge b/c i have seen instances where one case_number has two different juvenile_nbr's attached to it; not sure if we can use these data
tcs_charges_de_dup <- tcs_charges %>% 
    filter(!is.na(case_id)==TRUE,
         !is.na(id)==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(case_number = case_id) %>% 
  distinct(id,case_number,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(current_charge_classification_clean = ifelse(str_starts(current_offense,"712A"),"Status",current_offense_classification))


# de-dup dispositions file -- using case_id (same as 'case_number' in tcs_cases and 'id' (which is "Unique ID for the record.")); no records dropped -- will have to further de-dup by disposition later

# looks like there are some pure dups
tcs_dispositions_de_dup <- tcs_dispositions %>% 
    filter(!is.na(case_id)==TRUE,
         !is.na(name_nbr)==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(case_number = case_id,
                juvenile_nbr= name_nbr) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_nbr,case_number,charge_count,charge_count,id,dispo_dt,event_nbr,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(id = as.character(id))
  

# de-dup placements file -- using case_id (same as 'case_number' in tcs_cases and 'id' (which is "Unique ID for the record.")); no records dropped 

# looks like there are some pure dups
tcs_placements_de_dup <- tcs_placements %>% 
    filter(!is.na(case_id)==TRUE,
         !is.na(name_nbr)==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(case_number = case_id,
                juvenile_nbr= name_nbr) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_nbr,case_number,place_begin_date,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(unique_placement_id = paste0(juvenile_nbr,case_number,place_begin_date))
```

## Analysis Outline

**Placement Counts**

**Placement count and placements per 'case' over time**

* By pre-/post-adjudication

* By placement type

* By charge category

* By placement history

*	By race/ethnicity (RRI using MI population juvenile race/ethnicity data for pertinent counties)

* By age

* By gender

**Length of Stay**

**Mean and median length of stay over time** 

* By pre-/post-adjudication

* By placement type

* By charge category

* By placement history

*	By race/ethnicity (with t-tests for statistical significance of differences in means)

* By age

* By gender

**Other**

* There appears to be both "special cost" and "per diem" fields in the placement file

## Basic Sample Descriptives, Placement and Charge Data

<br>

#### Placement N's: Unique Placement Records by Year of Case, cases filed 2016-2020  (TCS pull was for "Case Filing Years Included - 2016-2020")

Note: Placements in this table are individual placements, not grouped by individual or case
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### create overall placement count denominator for % in cross-tabs
unique_placement_id_n <- n_distinct(tcs_placements_de_dup$unique_placement_id)

### all -- grouped by year
tcs_placements_year <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(case_year)==TRUE, 
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  group_by(case_year) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Year of Case` = case_year) %>% 
  mutate(`Year of Case` = as.character(`Year of Case`))

### all -- overall
tcs_placements_year_overall <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(case_year)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Year of Case` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable
tcs_placements_year_table <- rbind(tcs_placements_year,tcs_placements_year_overall)

### print table via kableextra
kable(tcs_placements_year_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(6, bold = TRUE)
```

#### Placement N's: Unique Placements by County (County Court), cases filed 2016-2020 

Note: Placements in this table are individual placements, not grouped by individual or case

Question: Do all Michigan counties have their own court? We don't appear to have county of residence for youth so if multiple counties share one court, they would be grouped together here. We have one extra county -- GOGEBIC -- in the case data but not in the placement data
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### clean county name
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(county_court_name = str_to_title(tc_sreport_courtname))
         
### create overall placement count denominator for % in cross-tabs
unique_placement_id_n <- n_distinct(tcs_placements_de_dup$unique_placement_id[!is.na(tcs_placements_de_dup$county_court_name)==TRUE])

### all -- grouped by placement type
tcs_placements_place_type <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(county_court_name)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  group_by(county_court_name) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`County Court` = county_court_name) %>% 
  mutate(`County Court` = as.character(`County Court`))

### all -- overall

  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(county_court_name)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`County Court` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable

### print table via kableextra
kable(tcs_placements_place_type_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
```

#### Charge N's: Unique Placements by Placement/Facility Type, cases filed 2016-2020 

Note: Charges in this table are individual charges, not grouped by individual or case. These are not yet linked to placements -- this is simply the universe of charges in the TCS data. 

```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
# From TCS code book: Current Offense Classification - C/Civil Infraction, F/Felony, M/Misdemeanor, S/Statute, H/High Misdemeanor, O/Other, V/Civil-Other, R/Ordinance, Z/Notice for Advisories
tcs_charges_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(current_offense_classification_clean = case_when(
    current_offense_classification %in% c("C","V") ~ 1,
    current_offense_classification == "F" ~ 2,
    current_offense_classification == "M" ~ 3,
    current_offense_classification == "S" ~ 4,
    current_offense_classification == "H" ~ 5,
    current_offense_classification == "R" ~ 6,
    current_offense_classification == "Z" ~ 7,
    current_offense_classification == "O" ~ 8,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    current_offense_classification_clean = factor(current_offense_classification_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8),
         labels = c("Civil","Felony", "Misdemeanor","Statute","High Misdemeanor","Ordinance","Notice for Advisories","Other"))) %>% ### use factor function to assign labels to values)
  mutate(unique_charge_id = paste0(id,case_number))

### create overall placement count denominator for % in cross-tabs
unique_charge_id_n <- n_distinct(tcs_charges_de_dup$unique_charge_id[!is.na(tcs_charges_de_dup$current_offense_classification_clean)==TRUE])

### all -- grouped by placement type
tcs_charge_type <- tcs_charges_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_charge_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(current_offense_classification_clean)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  group_by(current_offense_classification_clean) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_charge_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_charge_id)/unique_charge_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Charge Classification` = current_offense_classification_clean) %>% 
  mutate(`Charge Classification` = as.character(`Charge Classification`))

### all -- overall
tcs_charge_type_overall <- tcs_charges_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_charge_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(current_offense_classification_clean)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_charge_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_charge_id)/unique_charge_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Charge Classification` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable
tcs_charge_type_table <- rbind(tcs_charge_type,tcs_charge_type_overall)

### print table via kableextra
kable(tcs_charge_type_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(6, bold = TRUE)
```

## Codebooks

<br>

#### Cases
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### disable scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

### import variable labels from 'CSG_TCS_DataDictionary FINAL'
cases_labels <- readxl::read_xlsx(file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "CSG_TCS_DataDictionary FINAL.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names,
  sheet ="Cases", range = "B2:C110") %>% 
  mutate(data_column = make_clean_names(data_column))

### get descriptive statistics and select those of interest
cases_descriptives <- tcs_cases_de_dup %>% 
  describe(.,
           check = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(data_column = row.names(.)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  select(data_column,"n","min","max","mean") %>% 
  mutate(data_column = stringr::str_replace(data_column,"\\*",""))

### add stats to label 
cases_codebook <- left_join(cases_descriptives,cases_labels,by="data_column") %>% 
  select(data_column,tcs_definition=definition,everything())

### print table via kableextra
kable(cases_codebook, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), 
                row_label_position = "l") 
```

## Main Questions (out to Laura/relevant staff)

1.	Construction of ‘juvenile_nbr’ in ‘cases’ data file and ‘name_nbr’ in in ‘dispositions’ and ‘placements’ data files:
a.	These appear to all be the same column – is this column created just from a youth’s name? If so, should we use it in together with one of the age variables – such as ‘defendant_age_at_filing’ – to uniquely identify one youth (essentially a roundabout way of using name and DOB)? Any caution against this approach?
b.	I see a small number of ‘juvenile_nbr’ values of 0 – I have initially dropped these records as they don’t appear to the same individual. Is that correct? 


2.	In looking through the raw data, there appear to be instances in which one ‘case_number’/’caseid’ (these appear to be the same field) is shared by more than one ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’. Why would this be the case? And is the joint use of both ‘case_number’/’caseid’ and ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’ the best way to uniquely identify a single case?
a.	What is the definition/business rule for ‘case_number’/’caseid’? When are two offenses grouped as one ‘case_number’ and when would they appear as separate cases? 


3.	For our analysis of placement data in the TCS transfer, we are hoping to merge 'cases', 'charges', 'dispositions', and 'placements' together. Is this possible/advisable? 
a.	It appears as though there are ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’s and ‘case_number’/’caseid’s which appear in the ‘cases’ and ‘placements’ data tables, but not in the ‘charges’ data table. Do you all have any initial ideas for why this may be? 
b.	In general, it looks like we would merge these data files using ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’ and ‘case_number’/’caseid’ (and then ‘id’ can additionally be used to link ‘charges’ and ‘dispositions’ – does this make sense? Are there better ways to determine primary keys, de-duplicate (if need be), and merge? 


4.	What is the difference between `case_year` (noted as the "Year the case was filed.") and `year` (noted as "Year of the caseload being run/reported.")? Why does the data dictionary indicate that `year` "Must be included in some form to link tables" but not `case_year`?


5.	Is there a code book/data dictionary available for column values – particularly for race/ethnicity, event_nbr, dispo_event_nbr, sequence_nbr, case_type


6.	What is `ordertype` in the ‘placements’ data file? Many records with value of `ORD` as opposed to `PCN` are missing either start dates and/or end dates – why is this the case?
